a preposition construed with the genitive, dative, and accusative. Wellauer and Linwood have correctly arranged the Aeschylean examples, partly following others, both grammarians and lexicographers.
ἐπί with the genitive in a local sense, which the Latins express by the prepositions in, iuxta, ad, per, supra. Of the place in which something is.
ἐπί with the dative in a local sense.
Closely related to this use is that ἐπί is said of an action directed against someone, corresponding to Latin contra: on which see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1513.
ἐπί used of time can be rendered in Latin by post.
Frequent is the use of the preposition in expressions indicating either purpose or result: on which see at length in Thes. vol. 3 p. 1514 ff.
